key_insight: mmRUDEs make neural constitutive laws more stable, thermodynamically admissible, and interpretable by combining a frame-indifferent tensor backbone with multi-mode corrections and constrained training.
engineering_relevance: The framework improves reliable extrapolation for complex polymer and process flows, making data-driven rheology more usable in CFD and soft-material processing design.
method: Log-compress input invariants and use a split-network architecture to improve conditioning.
Apply a differentiable projection layer to enforce the Clausius--Duhem inequality at each time step.
Summarize learned tensor-basis contributions with the new “rheome” for interpretability.
evidence_signal: The models were trained on LAOS data for both a synthetic multi-mode Giesekus system and an entangled silicone polymer melt, and then tested successfully on unseen shear, stress-growth, and extensional flows.
watch_item: The added constraints and architecture still need careful implementation and validation to avoid over-constraining the model or limiting expressiveness on other material classes.
paper_title: Stable and Interpretable Multi-Mode Rheological Universal Differential Equations (mmRUDEs) for Data-Driven Constitutive Modeling
